title: Learned harmonic-panel BIE (HarmonicPanelBIE): 13-parameter PDE-conforming decoder

model.name: harmonic_panel_bie
model.structure: kappa = c1*Re(zeta^-1) + sum_{k=0..3} d_k*Re(zeta^k), zeta = n.r + i nxr; exact straight-panel quadrature (signed subtended angle + entire antiderivatives); p=8 drive-linear Richardson density solve through 0.5I + K; analytic constant lift

H1_solve_only.verdict: refuted: architecture alone adds no trace-consistency pressure

H1c_soft_kernel_harmonicity.verdict: refuted: penalty buys ~2x, mechanism needs exact harmonicity

H1d_exact_harmonicity_midpoint_quadratur.verdict: refuted: singular kernels need singular quadrature; free-form MLPs win by learning quadrature-mollified near-fields

minimal_10_parameters.note: regular_orders=0; higher regular orders unnecessary at 1000 steps

steps_3000.note: approaches the analytic oracle (id 0.003, freq 0.060); c1 within 0.7% of -1/(2*pi) - the 1000-step gap is optimization, not representation

resolution_transfer_seed17.note: trained at 64 panels; evaluation error decreases monotonically under refinement

caveats: 2D interior Dirichlet Laplace only; the harmonic Laurent basis is Laplace-specific (3D analogue: solid harmonics x Legendre in n.r_hat with exact triangle quadrature)
dense O(Nq*Ns) evaluation and O(p*Ns^2) solve; at scale the c1 term is the classical double layer so standard FMM/H-matrix acceleration applies verbatim
collocation-residual trace metric certifies solver convergence, not boundary fidelity, unless the imposed jump matches the kernel (self-consistent at c1=-1/(2*pi))
single-machine artifacts under /tmp/h1_learned_bie; not yet reproduced elsewhere

iteration_2_neumann.question: does kernel-basis + exact panel quadrature + learned drive-linear solve transfer to a different BC/jump structure?
iteration_2_neumann.implementation: evaluate_flux + build_neumann_domain_sample (exact analytic flux, discrete compatibility enforced, targets gauge-fixed to boundary-measure mean); NeumannHarmonicPanelBIE (adds c0*Re log zeta single-layer term with branch-safe exact panel integrals incl. self-panel L(log(L/2)-1); Neumann trace K' = n.grad(influence) via autograd; output anchored to its own exact boundary-trace mean, query-independent); --problem neumann in train.py; 13 new tests
structural_findings: orientation gauge matters: with T = -1/2 I + K' and alpha init +1, Richardson anti-converges at small kernel and SGD exploits solver divergence as a ~25x gain (learned kernel ~0, ID 0.081 in-sample, freq-OOD 0.268) - a degenerate optimum. Fix is the c=-1 gauge (T = +1/2 I + K', oracle c0 = -1/(2*pi)), a convention choice, not a tuned constant. General rule: place the zero-kernel init in the solver's convergent regime.
Neumann optimization is ~3x slower than Dirichlet: validation rises (~3.4 at step 250) before descending - an early landscape barrier while kernel and solve co-adapt

steps_3000.note: freq-OOD == ID: uniform operator behavior; c0 at 90% of oracle and still converging (validation monotone 0.88->0.12 over steps 1000-3000)

direct_p0_control.note: value-interpolator signature: good ID, poor frequency transfer

iteration_2_neumann.verdict: framework transfers; BC change costs optimization time, not structure

steps_10000_seed17.note: analytic-oracle-level accuracy uniformly across all splits including unseen frequencies; c0 within 1.8% of -1/(2*pi)

seeds_29_43_at_3000.note: same slow transit as seed 17 (0.12 at 3000); destination established by the 10k run

iteration_3_parametric_conditioning.question: should a global PDE parameter enter through the kernel basis (parameter-dependent fundamental solutions) or through learned coefficient conditioning?
iteration_3_parametric_conditioning.testbed: screened_laplace.py: exact Bessel-series Dirichlet problems for lap(u) - kappa^2 u = 0 on randomized disks; dimensionless kappa_tilde = kappa*R in global_data; train kappa in [0.5,2], OOD-high [3,5], OOD-low [0.05,0.3], unseen modes {4,5,6}; Gauss-16 panel quadrature for the K0/K1 kernels (documented numerical knob; zeroed self-panel breaks exact resolution transfer, noted)
findings: physics-in-basis gives exact operator fidelity (PDE residual 0 vs 1.65 = E[kappa_tilde^2] for the wrong basis, which measures precisely the operator mismatch) and the best parameter-OOD transfer with 10 parameters

each basis generalizes toward its own asymptotic regime: the harmonic conditioner wins the kappa->0 limit (0.0035) because harmonic IS that limit; Yukawa models blow up there as K0 diverges logarithmically
learned conditioning absorbs in-distribution numerical imperfections (0.0005; it learns the kappa-dependence of the zeroed self-panel term) but never extrapolates
a union basis does NOT rescue parameter-OOD: coefficient selection itself must extrapolate (union ood_low 25.0 despite containing the basis that solves it)
torch.special.modified_bessel_k0/k1 have no autograd derivatives; custom Functions with the analytic recurrences added (nested-derivative test)
iteration_3_parametric_conditioning.design_rule: the operator parameter must enter analytically through the fundamental-solution basis; learned conditioning is for in-distribution numerics, not physics extrapolation

iteration_4_pruning.protocol: 3000 steps, seed 17, early bank; ablations of HarmonicPanelBIE motivated by observed evidence (uniform learned relaxations; minimal variant winning at 1000 steps)

shared_alpha_3p.note: identical to minimal to 4 decimals: sharing the relaxation is lossless; d0 ~ 0 so effectively TWO scalars (c1, alpha) carry the solution operator; c1 within 0.5% of -1/(2*pi)

p2_solve_4p.note: 2 Richardson steps under-converge the density; the kernel inflates (c1 -0.1705) to compensate; solve depth is a numerical-convergence knob, keep p=8

confirmation_3seed_reference_bank.protocol: 3000 steps, seeds 17/29/43, eval seed 97000037, 64 cases (same bank as all headline comparisons)
confirmation_3seed_reference_bank.note: 3 parameters; seed spread ~30x tighter than larger variants; c1 within 0.8% of -1/(2*pi) on every seed; vs same-bank references: mesh_transformer 0.458 (136k params), pair_kernel 0.107 (19k), 13-param harmonic BIE 0.068 at 1000 steps

iteration_7_kernel_decoder_fix.change: MeshTransformer(query_decoder='kernel'): dense operator-conditioned pair-kernel query decoder (kernel_decoder.py) replacing the separable moment decoder; dictionary = exact-quadrature double-layer member (2D subtended angle / 3D solid angle, brute-force-verified) + polynomial {1,b,a} + 8-member MLP of joint pair invariants; coefficients from source operator-state invariants (encoder as conditioner); kernel never reads drive in linear mode; bitwise query independence via row-stable reductions

mesh_transformer_kernel.resolution_transfer: 0.322 -> 0.032 over 32->256 panels (discretization-convergent; moment decoder flat at ~0.27)

iteration_7_kernel_decoder_fix.spectral_fix_documented_in_tests: paired random-weight ring test: moment decoder m>=3 content <= 2e-11 (ceiling), kernel decoder >= 1e-6 (lifted); 180 core + 187 example tests pass, 11 contract tests parametrized over both decoders
caveats: seed-17, 1000 steps, early bank; 3-seed 3000-step reference-bank rows running on Brev
interior Laplacian ~1.0: PDE-agnostic smooth member is not harmonic; freq-OOD 0.12 achieved WITHOUT operator fidelity
on-boundary trace diagnostic (~1.6) reflects the singular member's discontinuity at the boundary; near-boundary interior error is 0.033

kernel_dictionary_only.note: kernel_mlp_members=0: exact double-layer + polynomial members only

reference_bank_3seed_3000steps.finding_dictionary_selection_tension: freq-OOD degraded 0.12(@1k steps)->0.49(@3k) for the full kernel decoder; ablating the smooth MLP members restores 0.0713 with IDENTICAL ID (0.0409 vs 0.0399) — unstructured smooth members are ID-neutral and OOD-destructive at this capacity; structured members + operator conditioning extrapolate. Caveat: the singular member is Laplace-family structure; on other PDE families the dictionary needs more members and the smooth member may earn its place (untested).

iteration_8_liouville_nonlinear_wall.question: Liouville (lap u + 2 e^u = 0) is homogeneous but nonlinear; all drive-linear models tied at ~0.79 ID (superposition wall; boundary_mean floor 1.06). The kernel-basis query decoder in zero_preserving_nonlinear field mode reads drive invariants, so it is NOT drive-linear. Does it break the wall, and do unstructured MLP members earn their place on a nonlinear PDE?
iteration_8_liouville_nonlinear_wall.setup: liouville.py, 1500 steps, seed 17, cuda (A100), same data protocol as prior Liouville baselines
findings: Wall broken: nonlinear kernel decoder reaches ~0.40 ID vs 0.77 for the linear-arm control (which lands on the predicted ~0.79 superposition wall). OOD improves too (unseen geometry modes 0.77->0.59, stronger deformation 0.72->0.46).
Dictionary-selection finding extends to nonlinear PDEs: dictionary-only (mlp_members=0) matches or beats full MLP members on all three splits at 10k fewer parameters.
PDE residual stays high (2.3-3.0 vs harmonic-prediction score of exactly 2): the model fits the field without satisfying the strong-form PDE; consistent with L2-fit-only training.
caveats: Headline protocol: 1500 steps, constant LR, final-model eval - identical to the Liouville baseline protocol.
Longer training needs LR decay + best-checkpoint selection before it means anything (see replication_p2b).

findings: Wall break REPLICATES: at 1500 steps, worst nonlinear ID (0.564) < best linear ID (0.749) across all 3 seeds; linear mean 0.769 sits on the ~0.79 superposition wall, nonlinear arms mean ~0.47 (1.6x better), OOD splits improve similarly.

MLP-member question resolves to a TIE at 1500 steps (nl 0.464 vs nomlp 0.476, sd ~0.085): unstructured smooth members neither help nor hurt on Liouville; parsimony favors dictionary-only. Seed 17 alone (tie) and seed 18 alone (nl wins by 0.13) each mislead - replication was necessary.

5000-step constant-LR training is UNSTABLE: validation oscillates late (nomlp val 0.44->0.60->0.41). CORRECTION (2026-07-04): liouville.py already restores the best-validation checkpoint before the final eval, so the nomlp ID 1.337 vs val 0.410 gap is NOT final-vs-best-model - it is a 4-case validation vs 16-case eval gap on an unstable model (heavy-tailed per-case errors). Protocol gap remaining: no LR decay; headline numbers use the 1500-step fixed-compute protocol shared with all baselines.

iteration_9_screened_meshtransformer.question: Does kappa-tilde conditioning through the MeshTransformer operator encoder (global scalar "screening" -> operator tokens -> kernel-decoder coefficients) extrapolate parameter-OOD, and how does the full generalist architecture compare to the iteration-3 specialist pair-kernel BIEs? Also: do MLP members hurt geometry-OOD on a second linear PDE?
iteration_9_screened_meshtransformer.setup: screened_laplace.py, mesh_transformer_kernel (110,593 par, 8 MLP members) vs mesh_transformer_kernel_nomlp (105,121 par), 2000 steps, seeds 17/18/19, cuda A100. field_mode=linear; kappa-tilde = kappa*R enters ONLY as operator global scalar. Comparators: iteration_3 specialists at same steps/seed17.
findings: Generalist beats the harmonic-basis specialist ID by ~5x (0.012 vs 0.061) without knowing the PDE, staying within ~4x of exact-Yukawa-basis specialists (0.003) that do.

Graceful low-kappa degradation: Yukawa-basis specialists diverge catastrophically at low kappa (8.7-28, K0 log-divergence); MeshTransformer degrades to 0.03-0.05 - its harmonic-biased singular dictionary contains the kappa->0 limit. High-kappa: the exact-basis specialist wins (0.016 vs 0.18) - the expected specialist/generalist trade.

STRONGEST dictionary-selection replication: MLP members leave ID and kappa-OOD unchanged but destroy unseen-modes generalization 10x (0.184 vs 0.019), consistent across all 3 seeds. Third linear-PDE occurrence (Laplace freq-OOD 0.12->0.49; screened modes 0.019->0.184); on nonlinear Liouville they were merely neutral.

iteration_10_laplace3d_meshtransformer.question: Does the kernel-decoder MeshTransformer work in 3D unchanged (dimensional genericity), how does it fare on the shell topology-OOD tier where pure double-layer is deficient, and does the MLP-member pattern from 2D carry over?
iteration_10_laplace3d_meshtransformer.setup: laplace3d_study.py, mesh_transformer_kernel (110,561 par, BITWISE-identical count to 2D - channels are D-independent) vs _nomlp (105,089), 3000 steps, seeds 17-22 (6 seeds), cuda A100. Boundaries merged outer+inner -> single dirichlet (identity only geometric). Oracle reference: sphere 0.003, star 0.002, shell 0.753 (double-layer deficiency).
findings: Dimensional genericity holds end-to-end: same architecture, same param count, no core changes; 3D ID sphere/star ~0.02 (within ~6x of the exact-quadrature oracle).

Shell topology-OOD: both arms (medians 0.380 / 0.458) beat the double-layer oracle (0.753) - attention-conditioned coefficients partially overcome the representational deficiency; high seed variance (sd 0.20-0.33), some catastrophic nomlp seeds (1.17).

MLP-member pattern FLIPS in 3D: mlp8 equal-or-better on star 6/6 seeds, modes-OOD 5/6 (means 0.087 vs 0.119), shell means 0.448 vs 0.592. Opposite of 2D linear (10x destructive). Refined hypothesis: unstructured members hurt where the structured dictionary already spans the smooth corrections (2D poly family) and help where it spans less (3D). Testable: drop polynomial members in 2D (singular+MLP only) -> if OOD collapses, poly members are the structured span that makes MLPs redundant.
caveats: Seed variance on shell/modes is large; 6 seeds give direction, not tight CIs.
No LR decay (protocol parity with 2D benchmarks).

iteration_11_dictionary_ablation_2d.question: Which dictionary members carry the 2D kernel decoder? Pre-registered (research log): span hypothesis predicted (a) nopoly recovers ID but destroys freq-OOD, (b) singonly loses ID but stays OOD-stable.
iteration_11_dictionary_ablation_2d.setup: train.py reference protocol (3000 steps, seeds 17/29/43, reference capacity, dirichlet), arms: nopoly = singular+8MLP (109,733p, 9 members), singonly = singular only (104,261p, 1 member). Comparators: iteration-7 kernel_full (12 members) and kernel_dictionary_only (=nomlp, 4 members) at identical protocol.
findings: SINGULAR-ONLY WINS OUTRIGHT: best ID (0.0375) and freq-OOD statistically identical to sing+poly (0.0748 vs 0.0713, tight seed spread 0.073-0.076), best stronger_deformation (0.0774). The exact singular member + operator conditioning carries everything in 2D; polynomial members are dead weight, MLP members are actively harmful.

Prediction (a) half-confirmed: nopoly recovers ID (0.042) and freq-OOD is destroyed relative to structured arms (0.213) - but LESS than the full arm (0.49): MLP members hurt MORE when polynomial members are also present (unexpected interaction).

Prediction (b) REFUTED favorably: singonly lost nothing - the span hypothesis as stated is dead. Revised rule: in 2D, ALL smooth members are at best neutral; smooth structure comes from operator conditioning, not the member dictionary. 3D disentangler launched (p3b: 3D nopoly/singonly x 6 seeds) - if 3D singonly degrades, 3D genuinely needs smooth members; if not, prune everywhere.
caveats: Single capacity (reference); interaction effect (poly amplifying MLP harm) unexplained.

iteration_12_dictionary_ablation_3d.question: 3D disentangler for iteration 11: does 3D genuinely need smooth members (iteration-10 reading: MLPs modestly helpful), or does singular-only win everywhere once polynomial members are removed?
iteration_12_dictionary_ablation_3d.setup: laplace3d_study.py, nopoly = singular+8MLP (109,733p) and singonly (104,261p), 3000 steps, seeds 17-22, cuda A100; protocol identical to iteration 10.
findings: POLYNOMIAL MEMBERS WERE THE PROBLEM IN 3D TOO: dropping them improves every split ~2x (sphere 0.017->0.0095/0.0072, star 0.018->0.014/0.012, modes 0.087->0.051/0.064) and collapses shell-tier seed variance (sd 0.20-0.33 -> 0.025-0.042; no more catastrophic 1.17 seeds). The iteration-10 "MLP members help in 3D" reading was an artifact: MLPs partially compensated for polynomial-member harm.
Singular-only matches singular+MLP in 3D (sphere 0.0072 vs 0.0095, star 0.0121 vs 0.0141, modes 0.0637 vs 0.0511, shell median 0.377 vs 0.373) - no split shows a decisive MLP win.

UNIVERSAL RULE (2D + 3D Laplace): dictionary = the exact singular member only; all smooth structure through operator-conditioned coefficients. 3D singular-only now beats the double-layer oracle 2x on the shell tier (0.377 vs 0.753) with tight variance.
Universality checks in flight (p3cd): screened singonly (kappa-conditioning must survive poly removal) and Liouville nl_singonly (wall break must survive full pruning).

iteration_13_singonly_universality.question: Does the singular-only rule extend to (a) screened Laplace (kappa-conditioning must survive poly removal) and (b) nonlinear Liouville (wall break must survive full pruning)?

screened_singonly_2000steps.finding: CONFIRMED and improved: singular-only is best-in-class on screened too (best ID and lowK, modes tie with sing+poly). Conditioning carries the kappa-dependence with a one-member dictionary.

liouville_nl_singonly_1500steps.finding: CATASTROPHIC FAILURE: ID 0.96/36.5/2.30 (seed 18 diverged). In zero-preserving-nonlinear field mode the polynomial members are LOAD-BEARING; removing them destabilizes training entirely.

iteration_13_singonly_universality.refined_rule: Drive-LINEAR operation: dictionary = exact singular member only; operator conditioning carries all smoothness (2D Laplace, screened, 3D Laplace all best-in-class). NONLINEAR field mode: smooth polynomial members are load-bearing for the drive-nonlinear correction; MLP members remain prunable everywhere. Open: is the nonlinear failure representational or optimization instability? LR-decay discriminator queued (if cosine decay rescues nl_singonly to ~0.46, poly members were an optimization crutch; if not, they are representational).

iteration_14_scalar_only_2d.question: Do the vector (1o) channels earn their complexity? Scalar-only mode ablates oriented state transport between cells (normals still enter via scalar Gram invariants and decoder pair invariants).
iteration_14_scalar_only_2d.setup: train.py reference protocol, 3000 steps, seeds 17/29/43. Arms: mesh_transformer_kernel_singonly_scalar (41,941p, -59.8%) and mesh_transformer_kernel_scalar (full dict, 46,273p, -58.1%).
findings: VECTOR CHANNELS NOT LOAD-BEARING ON 2D LAPLACE: scalar singular-only (41,941p) matches vector-ful singular-only (104,261p) within ~5-15% on every split at 60% fewer params; similarity covariance stays at machine precision (2.7e-7).
The MLP-member freq destruction persists in scalar mode (0.32) but is smaller than vector-ful (0.49) - less capacity to overfit.
Caveat: 2D circle-family geometry may simply not need oriented transport; 3D, screened, and especially the encoder-stress benchmarks (multi-hop coupling) are the discriminating tests, queued.

VECTORS ARE LOAD-BEARING OFF PLAIN 2D LAPLACE: screened ID degrades 2-3x (0.028 vs 0.0099); 3D sphere degrades 3.4x (0.0244 vs 0.0072), star 1.9x. But modes-OOD is UNCHANGED-or-better and shell is identical with TIGHTER variance (sd 0.013 vs 0.042) - more evidence shell error is representational (missing single-layer member), not encoder capacity.
Confound: 42k vs 104k params. Capacity-matched wide-scalar control (52/76 scalar dims, rank 18, 105,301 params) built and launched (p4e) to disentangle oriented-transport from width.

wide_scalar_capacity_control.setup: scalar-only widened to 105,301 params (52/76 dims, rank 18) = +1% of vector-ful; 2D/screened/3D
wide_scalar_capacity_control.verdict: CONCLUSIVE - VECTORS ARE LOAD-BEARING, NOT WIDTH: capacity-matched scalar does NOT recover the gap (3D sphere 0.024 vs 0.0072 vector-ful = 3.3x; screened ID 0.024 vs 0.0099 = 2.5x); 2D stays at parity. Oriented inter-cell state transport is genuine physics capacity off plain 2D geometry. Component eval closed: keep the vector channels.

iteration_15_transolver_comparison.question: Fair-ground comparison against the strongest physics-agnostic attention architecture (Transolver, Wu et al. ICML 2024; faithful port verified against the official repo; steel-man adaptations: shared boundary+query token sequence gives it MORE interaction than MeshTransformer gets; same normalization as our baselines). The thesis ablation: what does building BIE structure into attention buy?
iteration_15_transolver_comparison.protocol: train.py reference protocol (streaming generation, 1 case/step, AdamW 3e-4, identical to all MT runs), seeds 17/29/43. transolver_matched=103,053p (vs MT singonly 104,261p), transolver_native=2,809,409p (27x). Step curve 3k/10k/30k for native.
findings: Data efficiency: at matched params and compute (3k steps) Transolver ID=0.769 vs MT 0.0375 (20x). Native capacity (27x params): 0.608@3k -> 0.262@10k -> 0.119@30k - still 3.2x worse than MT-at-3k after 10x the compute; power-law slope suggests ~300k+ steps to close ID.

Architectural gaps that training does NOT close: freq-OOD saturates ~0.46 (vs 0.075) - physics-agnostic attention does not extrapolate the drive spectrum; similarity covariance stuck at ~0.08-0.25 across all budgets (vs 3e-7) - 5-6 orders of magnitude equivariance gap.

Honest scope notes: streaming small-data regime is our claimed strength and Transolvers published regime (large fixed datasets, many epochs) is not tested here (dataset-backed training arm queued on the FEM catalog); Transolver retains advantages out of our scope: volumetric/piecewise inputs, linear O(N) scaling at industrial N.

screened_and_3d_extension.setup: In-tree Transolver (matched, 103,117p screened / 103,245p 3D), kappa as constant token channel (steel-man), D-generalized adapter; identical protocols; h100-3.
findings: Matrix complete: screened ID 0.773 vs MT singonly 0.0099 (78x); 3D sphere 0.402 vs 0.0072 (56x), star 0.414 vs 0.0121 (34x), shell 0.529 vs 0.377 (1.4x).

The gap narrows exactly where the MeshTransformer is itself representation-limited (shell) and explodes where its structure pays (smooth tiers) - consistent with the thesis-ablation reading across every suite.

iteration_16_single_layer_member.pre_registered_prediction: Shell tier improves dramatically (double-layer flux deficiency on multiply-connected domains); simply-connected tiers unchanged.
iteration_16_single_layer_member.implementation: Exact single-layer member: 2D Hess-Smith segment closed form, 3D per-edge asinh + solid-angle form; quadrature validated to ~1e-14; +276 params (singpair = 104,537, exactly two exact singular members).
findings_so_far: PREDICTION FAILING ON BOTH HALVES: shell NOT fixed (0.305/0.368/0.704 - median matches singonly, one unstable seed); 2D freq-OOD REGRESSED 2-4x (0.17-0.27 vs 0.075). Sphere improved slightly (0.004-0.008).

Refined insight: any member with a smooth FAR-FIELD - even an exact singular one - is abused by SGD to absorb ID error at the cost of extrapolation, because the conditioned coefficients are unconstrained; in classical BIE the single-layer density is determined by the boundary system, not freely fit.

Pending discriminator: p5b multi_body (2D holes, genuine winding content in the data) - if singpair helps THERE while hurting simply-connected freq-OOD, the design answer is a TOPOLOGY-GATED dictionary: member set selected by the number of boundary loops (Betti number) - a discrete physical gate, not a learned choice.

multi_body_head_to_head_partial.reading: TOPOLOGY-GATE CONFIRMED (seed 17): on the multiply-connected family the single-layer member halves error on every split, and WITHOUT it the MeshTransformer loses to the pair-kernel control (0.140 vs 0.097) - the flux deficiency was binding. Combined with the simply-connected freq-OOD regression, the design rule: include the single-layer member iff the domain has interior boundary loops (Betti-gated dictionary). Seeds 18/19 + deep_cavity control pending.

verdict: MULTI-BODY (3 seeds, CLOSED): singpair sweeps all 12 split-seed comparisons (means ID 0.065 vs 0.115, narrow_gap 0.160 vs 0.246, single_body 0.102 vs 0.153, unseen_charge 0.087 vs 0.153) and beats the pair-kernel control everywhere; WITHOUT the single layer the MeshTransformer loses to pair_kernel in-distribution (0.115 vs 0.097) - the flux deficiency binds on genuinely multiply-connected data.

DEEP-CAVITY (2 seeds): single layer helps hard simply-connected geometry too (deep_slot 0.27 vs 0.40 means, ID 0.067 vs 0.098) - so the gate is not purely Betti: the second exact member helps wherever geometry is hard and hurts extrapolation only on the easy star bank (freq-OOD 0.075->0.21). Refined rule: two exact singular members as the default dictionary for hard geometry; the star-bank regression is the honest cost.

NEW FAILURE (stress-test target): BOTH MT arms lose to the 19k-param pair_kernel on deep_slot OOD (0.21-0.45 vs 0.265 at seed level) while winning ID - the architecture generalizes to deeper slots no better than a dense pair map.

deep_cavity_final_n3.update: Deep-cavity closed at 3 seeds: singpair deep_slot mean 0.240 now MATCHES/BEATS pair_kernel (0.265) - the earlier "MT loses on deep_slot" failure was specifically the singonly arm (mean 0.393). With both exact members the architecture is competitive on the hardest OOD tier; the failure claim is downgraded to "singonly insufficient on hard geometry".

iteration_17_fixed_dataset_regime.question: Does the Transolver comparison hold in ITS published regime (large fixed dataset, many epochs, best-checkpoint) - and does the MeshTransformer survive solver-verified labels whose BC traces are outside any harmonic construction?
iteration_17_fixed_dataset_regime.setup: dataset_train.py on star_random_trace v1 (4,608 FEM cases, P2 solver rel-err ~1e-8, random Fourier Dirichlet traces in arc length; 2,304 train), 15 epochs (~35k case-visits), AdamW 3e-4 streaming-parity protocol, seeds 17/29.
findings: Comparison holds on Transolvers home turf: matched-param Transolver ID 0.126-0.136 vs MT singonly 0.016-0.017 (7.7x); native (27x params) 0.062-0.070 (3.8x); trace-frequency-OOD gap ~10x (0.089-0.131 vs 0.010-0.013). Both fairness regimes now tested; the steel-man is complete.

External validity: MT reaches 0.017 ID / 0.010 freq-OOD on FEM-verified labels with BC traces decoupled from harmonic reachability - the architecture is not exploiting manufactured-solution structure.

iteration_18_encoder_depth.status: multi_body n=2: enc0 ~ enc1 ~ enc2 confirmed on Dirichlet stress family; mixed-BC discriminator (iteration_19) shows where depth DOES matter.
iteration_18_encoder_depth.finding_preliminary: enc0 (NO boundary self-attention, 59,385 params) MATCHES the full 2-layer singpair on multi_body seed 17 (ID 0.073 vs 0.070). If this holds, boundary attention is dead weight on every current benchmark and the model collapses to lift -> conditioned 2-member singular decode. THEORY (pre-registered): Dirichlet double-layer density is a second-kind Fredholm solve dominated by the local 1/2-identity term, so weak nonlocality is expected; the attention-necessity test belongs on mixed/Neumann BC problems where the solve is genuinely nonlocal.

iteration_19_mixed_bc_discriminator.pre_registered: Mixed-BC Cauchy solves are genuinely nonlocal (vs half-identity-dominated all-Dirichlet) -> encoder depth should matter on mixed where it did not on Dirichlet. Only genuinely mixed tier: shell (inner Dirichlet trace, outer Neumann flux; per-boundary assignment).
iteration_19_mixed_bc_discriminator.setup: mixed_bc_study.py, mt_singpair_mixed{,_enc1,_enc0} (104,713/82,137/59,561p), 3000 steps, seeds 17/18/19, splits shell_mixed + shell_mixed_fine (resolution OOD).
findings: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED IN DIRECTION, WITH A PARSIMONY TWIST: enc0 degrades on mixed BCs (shell_mixed mean 0.079 vs 0.049; catastrophic seed 18: 0.112/0.182) while enc1 matches enc2 (0.051 vs 0.049) - attention earns its keep exactly where the Fredholm structure is nonlocal, and ONE encoder layer suffices. Depth-0 is unreliable (seed instability) rather than uniformly worse.
Physics note: shell_mixed at 0.049 is 7x EASIER than all-Dirichlet shell (0.37) - giving the outer flux explicitly removes the winding-inference difficulty.
Caveats: single mixed geometry tier (per-boundary BC assignment); drive_layers held at 1 in all arms - if a sharper claim is needed, sweep drive depth (nonlocal DATA coupling lives in drive blocks).

iteration_20_scale_ladder.setup: scale_study.py, 3D singpair arm with operator_layers=1 (81,961p; the iteration-19 sufficient depth), A100 80GB: cost grid (320-20480 tris x 1e3-1e5 queries, OOM-guarded, encode/decode timed separately) + resolution transfer (train subdiv 2, zero-shot 2/3/4).

extrapolation_product_scope.what_breaks_first: training memory breaks first: one forward+backward at product scope extrapolates to ~742 GiB (9x an 80 GiB A100) because autograd retains the dense O(Nq*Ns) pair activations of the kernel decode; gradient checkpointing over query chunks (or a hierarchical decode backend) is required before product-scale training is possible; inference stays chunk-bounded at ~79.4 GiB and is limited by wall-clock instead: ~541 s per forward (~1355 s forward+backward), the dense O(Nq*Ns) decode

notes: encode_ms shows no growth with boundary size over the measured range (separable-moment encoder, O(Ns) per layer): the measurements are kernel-launch-overhead dominated and the fitted exponent is a floor artifact, not architecture cost; the encoder is not the wall

the fitted forward_backward_ms extrapolation fell below the forward-only extrapolation (the forward+backward points that survive the paging exclusions are small and overhead-dominated on this device); it is suppressed in favor of the ideal O(Nq*Ns) entry

findings: Cost law confirmed: decode O(Q^0.97 S^0.96), R2=0.999 - the designed dense O(QS); encoder flat over the measured range (launch-overhead dominated; not the wall).

Product scope (1e5 boundary x 1e6 queries): TRAINING MEMORY BREAKS FIRST - one forward+backward extrapolates to ~742 GiB (9x an A100) because autograd retains dense pair activations. Named fixes: gradient checkpointing over query chunks (cheap, exact) or a hierarchical decode backend (FMM-style). Inference fits one A100 with chunking (~85 GB peak, ~9-16 min forward).
Resolution transfer (fully trained): sphere 0.0101/0.0155/0.0175 and star 0.0136/0.0196/0.0312 zero-shot across 16x resolution - the exact-quadrature transfer claim holds with mild degradation.

Efficiency gap found while profiling: PairInvariantFeatures.compute runs unconditionally in the dense hot loop even when the dictionary has no smooth members to consume it (~10 dead floats per pair on singpair/singonly arms) - a straightforward speed fix, queued.

iteration_21_fluid_families_pseudoscalar.setup: potential_flow.py: exterior potential flow (certified exterior conformal maps, freestream as global rank-1 drive vector + circulation scalar; target = disturbance STREAMFUNCTION, single-valued under circulation) and boundary_layer (manufactured two-scale field, near/far buckets). Controls are TRACE-INFORMED (exact disturbance trace as boundary_value); MT arms get raw {U, Gamma} only. 3000 steps, 3 seeds, H100 fleet.
iteration_21_fluid_families_pseudoscalar.finding: THE PSEUDOSCALAR WALL: MT arms at no-response (potential_flow ID 0.98-1.00, boundary_layer 0.91-1.04, all seeds) while trace-informed pair_kernel reaches 0.178/0.73. Gradient diagnostic: d(out)/d(freestream)=6359 - the path is alive. Root cause: the streamfunction is a 2D PSEUDOSCALAR (uniform-flow part is the wedge U^x = Ux*y - Uy*x); the type system builds scalars only from DOT products of polar vectors and cannot manufacture handedness from unhanded inputs - the architecture is enforcing its type contract, and the benchmark target violates it. Controls escape because the pseudoscalar-ness arrives baked into per-cell trace scalars. Circulation itself is a pseudoscalar (benchmark restricted to orientation-preserving similarities).
fix_paths: velocity vector output (polar, representable; = Euler multi-field step)
trace-driven MT variant (separates encode-solve difficulty from type mismatch)
2D pseudoscalar (0o) channels with wedge product (previously set aside; now has a concrete motivating failure)

iteration_22_representable_reformulation.setup: p10, 3000 steps, 3 seeds, H100s. Trace arms (MT given the same certified boundary trace as controls, predicting psi_d) and velocity arms (rank-1 output, exact dW/dz push-forward targets; first vector-output runs of the program).
findings: TRACE ARMS RESOLVE THE WALL COMPLETELY: singpair_trace ID 0.013 / geo 0.012 / wilder 0.045 / circulation-OOD 0.020 - 14x better than the pair-kernel control (0.178) given IDENTICAL data. The pseudoscalar wall was pure target-type mismatch; the architecture handles the exterior problem + circulation excellently in representable variables.

VELOCITY ARMS BREAK THE WALL AND EXPOSE A SECOND TYPE FINDING: ID 0.14 / geo 0.19, but circulation-OOD pinned at 0.646-0.649 across ALL arms and seeds. The vortex velocity is Gamma*x_perp/(2pi|x|^2): with Gamma typed as a TRUE scalar this product is axial - unrepresentable. The residual decomposes into representable potential flow (learned) + unrepresentable vortex flow (refused). Pre-registered Armijo criterion for the pseudoscalar (0o) extension is MET, precisely on the circulation component.
New stress axis: farfield_queries degrades for every arm (0.43-0.88; control 1.69) - radius extrapolation beyond the training annulus is open.
Rank-1 output path verified complete in core (first vector-output benchmark runs).

iteration_23_pseudoscalar_extension.design: First type-system extension: 2D pseudoscalar (0o) channels, rank token "0o", closed product set {v^w->0o wedge, p*v_perp->1 rotation, p*q->0e, s*p->0o}; pseudos ride the scalar moment machinery; bitwise-default (zero params/RNG at width 0); circulation declared 0o. Arms kernel_pseudo 138,665p / singpair_pseudo 132,641p (drive_pseudo_dim=8). 553 tests incl. reflection equivariance of every product and end-to-end model reflection tests.
iteration_23_pseudoscalar_extension.pre_registered_prediction: circulation-OOD joins ID; other splits unmoved.
findings: PREDICTION CONFIRMED AND EXCEEDED at 5 seeds: circulation-OOD 0.647 -> 0.037 (17x; joins ID at 0.028) - and the ENTIRE velocity field improves ~5x (ID 0.141->0.028, geo 0.191->0.041, wilder 0.264->0.131). Fresh control seeds (20/21) confirm the pinned floor. Interpretation: 2D potential-flow velocity is intrinsically parity-mixed (doublet angular structure carries both U.x and U^x content), so wedge invariants pay everywhere.
Parsimony holds under the extension: singpair (two exact members) remains the best dictionary in the pseudo setting.
farfield (radius extrapolation) unchanged (~0.7-0.8) - confirmed as a non-type open axis.
Scope: 0o is 2D-only and opt-in (3D analogue = axial vector, out of scope); NOT part of the default reference configuration.

iteration_24_intrinsic_gauge.design: Default scale gauge made intrinsic: reference_length_key=None derives L as the measure-weighted RMS boundary radius (radius of gyration, fp64, differentiable); explicit key remains a bitwise-preserved override. Makes scale equivariance UNCONDITIONAL (degree-1 homogeneity; no caller convention to drift).
findings: GAUGE NEUTRALITY at 3 seeds: intrinsic ID mean 0.0372 vs explicit 0.0375 - identical band; freq/geo likewise.
CONVENTION-DRIFT: explicit-key model degrades 4.64x under a 3x L_ref corruption at eval; the intrinsic model is BITWISE immune (the input no longer exists). Permanent demo test.
Similarity contract UNCONDITIONAL: paired covariance 2.9-3.1e-7 including 0.2x/5x scales.
Bonus latent bug found+fixed: pair-invariant einsum broke bitwise query independence for any L != 1 (1-ulp CUDA batched-GEMM drift masked by L=1 test data).

iteration_25_euler_bernoulli_multifield.design: First MULTI-FIELD benchmark: euler_bernoulli - exterior flow, targets {velocity rank-1, pressure rank-0}; pressure p*=(|U|^2-|u|^2)/2 is exactly drive-QUADRATIC (exact labels, no solver; velocity odd / pressure even under drive negation, verified exactly). Pre-registered second wall: a linear-mode arm is bitwise drive-odd, hence structurally zero pressure response. Multi-field output worked through core UNCHANGED.
findings: SECOND STRUCTURAL WALL CONFIRMED AT 5 SEEDS: linear-mode pressure pinned at exactly 1.000 on every split (bitwise drive-odd proof); nonlinear mode breaks it (0.210), and nonlinear+parity multiplies (0.063 pressure, 0.031 velocity - 5x/3x better than plain nl).

The 200-step amplitude blowup (circ-OOD 37-147) largely resolved with training: 3000-step circ-OOD 0.35 (pseudo) - drive-amplitude extrapolation remains the worst split but is no longer catastrophic; the pre-registered degree-grading hypothesis is demoted to a moderate-priority open item (Armijo: one-split gain).
The parity and nonlinearity mechanisms compose: their joint arm dominates every split.

iteration_26_stream_factorization.design: Two-stream operator/drive separation vs single-stream control (drive re-declared as operator features + unit-drive propagation; example-level wrapper, zero core changes; matched params within 0.03%). Control documented as measurement-only. Pre-registered H1 (ID parity on linear), H2 (two-stream wins freq-OOD), H3 (measure control contract violation).
findings: H1 SUPPORTED: two-stream wins Laplace ID by 3.6x seed-sd at matched params - the factorization costs nothing on linear problems; it helps.

H2 FALSIFIED (honest refutation of a motivating belief): structural drive-linearity did NOT buy freq-OOD (single-stream 0.179 vs 0.211, and more seed-stable). Frequency extrapolation comes from the dictionary/conditioning, not the linearity contract.
H3: the control learns APPROXIMATE linearity (zero-drive 0.038, superposition 0.042 - plateaus ~5 decades above the structural roundoff-exact contract).

LIOUVILLE: statistical tie (0.478+-0.097 vs 0.533+-0.145) - AND a misspecification insight: zero-preservation is only correct physics when the homogeneous problem has the zero solution; Liouville with zero Dirichlet data has u = log 4 != 0 inside, the structural contract pins the wrong value (two-stream zero-drive = 0 exactly; the free control learns 0.55-0.70). Structural priors need a per-problem correctness check.

iteration_27_farfield_strong_inference.design: Strong inference on the farfield_queries failure (0.67-0.88 all arms): three rival mechanisms, each with a pre-registered discriminator. Artifacts: farfield_inference_2026-07-04.json (+ annulus8 supplement).

verdicts.M1_annulus_coverage: AMBIGUOUS/PARTIAL: widening train annulus [1.05,4]->[1.05,8] cuts farfield 0.694->0.179 (74%) but stays 6.2x above ID even inside the new annulus - strong mitigation, not the cause.
verdicts.M2_member_decay: EXCLUDED: member basis exactly analytic on [4,12] (DL -1.9, SL +1/ln r); prediction SUPER-decays (exponent -24 vs exact -2) - opposite direction from member tails; the basis cannot out-decay r^-2 so the pathology cannot live there.
verdicts.M3_coefficient_extrapolation: SUPPORTED, smoking gun: output-projection sigmoid gate collapses at the training edge (0.52@r=1.1 -> 0.010@r=4 -> 2.3e-17@r=12; local exponents -13/-26/-51), imprinting identical collapse on direct and message parts. OUT-OF-SAMPLE CONFIRMATION: on the annulus-8 checkpoint the collapse onset MOVES to the new training edge - the pathology tracks the training boundary, not the dictionary.

iteration_27_farfield_strong_inference.process_note: verdict_m2 as first coded implemented only the magnitude half of its pre-registered rule; the directional qualifier (written in the docstring before measurement) flips it to EXCLUDED - disclosed; annulus-8 edge-tracking independently corroborates M3.
iteration_27_farfield_strong_inference.followup_prediction: Iteration 28: reparameterize/bound the radius-saturating gate -> far-field decay restored to ~r^-2 beyond the training annulus and farfield split drops substantially at UNCHANGED annulus; falsifier: no improvement means the gate is symptom, not cause.

iteration_28_bounded_gate.design: Fix attempt for the diagnosed gate collapse: compactify the output-projection gate inputs (v -> v/sqrt(1+|v|^2), s -> s/sqrt(1+s^2)); bounded pre-activation, no saturation regime; default-off knob, bitwise-preserved.
iteration_28_bounded_gate.pre_registered: far decay ~ -2; farfield < 0.35 supported / < 0.10 fixed; ID within 0.01.
iteration_28_bounded_gate.verdict: FALSIFIER FIRED - honest refutation: the gate fix worked as designed (smooth nonzero gate, no saturation) yet farfield got 4.3x WORSE. The collapse was LOAD-BEARING: it suppressed polynomially growing query-side direct-drive linear branches (vector_from_scalar 0.026@r=1.1 -> 1.45@r=12; lifted drive norms grow ~r-r^2, geometry vectors ~r). Root cause = the PAIR of unbounded radial dependences (saturating gate AND growing linear branches). Silver lining: bounded gates IMPROVE in-annulus accuracy (ID 0.0215 vs 0.0269, circ 0.018 vs 0.033).
iteration_28_bounded_gate.next: Iteration 29: bound the query-side inputs at the SOURCE (compactify the injected query position channel), so every learned coefficient sees bounded invariants and radial extrapolation is carried solely by the exactly-analytic kernel members.

iteration_29_source_bounded_query.design: Bound at the source: injected query position x -> x/sqrt(1+|x|^2) (equivariant compactification) so every learned coefficient sees bounded invariants; kernel members verified to read RAW positions (bitwise-pinned) - the physics path exact.
iteration_29_source_bounded_query.verdict: M3 EXCLUDED for the first time (coefficient traces flat to r=12; source-bounding did exactly what it claims); farfield 0.452 - between bars (partial). Residual is purely REPRESENTATIONAL (M2 survives): bounded != decaying - the direct-drive part converges to a direction-dependent constant (~0.24, exponent ~0) while the exact field decays r^-2, and the single-layer log-r tail (state norm 2.4 @ r=12) is fit by near-cancellation in-annulus. HONEST DECOMPOSITION: far-field error = coefficient extrapolation (fixed by construction) + missing decay structure (needs coverage [M1, 74%] or explicit structure).
iteration_29_source_bounded_query.next: Iteration 30 (4th rung): decaying radial multiplier on query-side direct-drive branches + monopole-controlled single-layer coefficients.

iteration_30_decay_structure.design: Fourth rung: (1) decaying_direct_drive - exact analytic envelope 1/(1+|x|^2) on the direct query-side drive path (2D exterior zero-flux velocity leading order = doublet r^-2; the direct drive may not outlive it); (2) monopole_free_single_layer - measure-weighted rank-one deflation of the SL member column (exact zero net charge per member -> log tail dead by construction for ANY coefficients; corollary: 2D log gauge cancels, deflated member exactly similarity invariant). Both opt-in, licensed for zero-net-flux exteriors only; no parameters added.
iteration_30_decay_structure.verdict: SUPPORTED (<0.35 bar met; not the <0.10 fully-fixed bar): 5.2x farfield improvement at UNCHANGED training annulus, beating the coverage lever (0.179), with ID and every side split improved. The four-rung ladder closes: coefficient extrapolation fixed by construction (source-bounding) + decay structure supplied by licensed exact physics (envelope + deflation). Remaining leak to <0.10: the r^-1 member tails' zero-circulation cancellation to r^-2 is still fitted.
iteration_30_decay_structure.five_seed_extension: seeds 18-21 launched (p19b) to close at the 5-seed bar.

five_seed_close.verdict: LADDER CLOSED AT 5 SEEDS: farfield mean 0.090 crosses the fully-fixed bar (<0.10) - 7.7x improvement at UNCHANGED training annulus (per-seed spread 0.036-0.147, two seeds above 0.10 - stated honestly). Every other split at best-ever levels for the family (ID 0.0174, circ 0.0168, geo 0.0303). The four physics-licensed knobs (bounded gates, bounded query source, r^-2 direct-drive envelope, monopole-free SL) compose into a strictly dominant configuration.

iteration_31_heads_vs_rank.design: Heads-versus-rank probe (pre-registered in studies/heads_rank_study.py): three singpair arms at fixed total score capacity H*(R0 + 2*R1) = 80 on the 2D Laplace reference bank, 3000 steps, seeds 17/29/43, iteration-26 finalist evaluation bank. One layer's pair-coefficient class depends only on the total, so any difference localizes in the per-head value/output structure. Rule: per arm and split, |3-seed mean delta vs reference| <= 2 * max(seed sd); all within -> heads are bookkeeping; any outside -> the per-head value/output structure carries a real effect.
findings: H8 IS BOOKKEEPING: at halved ranks (6/2) the 8-head arm matches the reference within tolerance on every split (largest |delta| 0.0050, on stronger_deformation vs its 0.0296 tolerance; ID delta -0.0024 vs 0.0050).

H1 IS NOT: the single-head arm (ranks 48/16, value/output maps unblocked) is decisively BETTER on interpolation (0.0413 vs 0.0485, delta -0.0072 vs tolerance 0.0050, i.e. 2.9x the larger seed sd) and directionally better on all four splits, with the FEWEST parameters of the three arms (104,123, -0.40%).
SEED STABILITY: h1 is also the most seed-stable arm (geometry sd 0.0018 vs reference 0.0070; freq-OOD sd 0.0158 vs 0.0523).

LOCALIZATION: score capacity was matched by construction, so the h1 gain prices the head-blocking of the value/output maps - blocking values into 4 aligned groups is a restriction that buys nothing measured here. The parsimony question opens in the FEWER-heads direction: one full-width head.
SCOPE: one PDE (2D Laplace), three seeds, one capacity point; h1's win is decisive under the pre-registered rule but is a 15% ID error reduction, not an order of magnitude.

iteration_32_one_head_cross_suite.design: One-head cross-suite confirmation of iteration 31 (pre-registered in studies/one_head_cross_suite.py before any run): capacity-preserving h1 variants (heads 1, scalar_rank 48, vector_rank 16; H*(R0+D*R1) fixed at the reference 4*(12+D*4) = 1*(48+D*16) in every D) on screened Laplace (mesh_transformer_kernel_singonly_h1, 2000 steps), potential-flow velocity (mesh_transformer_kernel_singpair_pseudo_h1, drive_pseudo_dim=8, 3000 steps), and 3D Laplace (mesh_transformer_kernel_singpair_h1, 3000 steps), 3 seeds (17/18/19) each, compared against the ARCHIVED h4 comparator runs (protocols matched run-for-run; nothing re-trained on the h4 side). Pre-registered flip rule: h1 matches-or-beats on a split iff mean(h1) - mean(h4) <= 2 * max(seed sd of the two arms); flip the reference configuration to one head iff every split of >= 2 suites matches-or-beats AND no split anywhere is a decisive loss; any decisive loss -> heads stay at 4 and iteration 31 is recorded as Laplace-specific.
iteration_32_one_head_cross_suite.session_artifacts: scratch/brev/results/p21_onehead (9 driver reports + aggregate.json), jobs p21_oh_*
findings: NO DECISIVE LOSS ANYWHERE: all 13 suite-split cells match-or-beat under the pre-registered tolerance; all three suites pass on every split; the falsifier did not fire.

THE ITERATION-31 WIN DID NOT TRAVEL: the 15% Laplace ID gain reappears nowhere - h1's 3-seed mean is directionally worse on 11 of 13 cells, and both exceptions are mode-OOD splits (screened unseen_modes -0.0006, 3D star_unseen_modes -0.0101). The cross-suite evidence is non-inferiority, not superiority.

CLOSEST CELLS, STATED PLAINLY: screened ID +0.0107 vs tolerance 0.0135 (1.6x the larger sd) and pf wilder_shapes +0.0304 vs 0.0589 (1.0x); several tolerances are widened by the h1 arm's OWN larger seed sd (the rule keys tolerance to max of the two sds), a bias worth naming - the noisier arm buys itself slack.

VERDICT - FLIP ON PARSIMONY, NOT ON SUPERIORITY: per the pre-registered rule the reference configuration flips to one full-width head (heads=1, scalar_rank=48, vector_rank=16): fewer heads, fewer parameters on every suite (-0.20%/-0.31%/-0.40%), one less architectural degree of freedom, and no split anywhere measurably worse. The flip lands in the documented reference configuration (book sec-reference-config, 1-layer singpair: 81,961 -> 81,547 params); the frozen benchmark capacity configs and every archived arm stay bitwise as recorded, per the program's comparability convention.

PSEUDO-SECTOR COMPOSITION CONFIRMED: the one-head trade composes with drive_pseudo_dim=8 unchanged (per-head pseudo split 8/heads goes 2 -> 8 exactly as the scalar channels); circulation_ood stays at the typed-circulation level (0.0476 vs 0.0371, within tolerance) - the iteration-23 fix survives the head change.
STANDING FALSIFIER: the flip reverts if any suite ever shows a decisive h1 loss; at three seeds these cells are within-tolerance ties, not proof of equivalence.

iteration_33_euler_rotational.design: Iteration 33: euler_rotational -- the first genuinely ROTATIONAL steady Euler family. omega = c^2 psi (vorticity linear in the streamfunction) => lap psi + c^2 psi = 0 (Helmholtz; Bessel J_m series on disks, the oscillatory sibling of screened's I_m/K_m); u = (psi_y, -psi_x) (psi pseudoscalar, u polar); pressure from the rotational Bernoulli relation H(psi) = -c^2 psi^2/2 (gauge H0=0): p = -c^2 psi^2/2 - |u|^2/2, exactly drive-quadratic. Targets {velocity rank-1, pressure rank-0}; drive = boundary velocity on cells; c~ = c R as a global operator scalar. All couplings kept strictly below the first disk Dirichlet eigenvalue j_{0,1} = 2.404826 (at eigenvalues the interior is not determined by boundary data). Pre-registered third structural wall: the linear arm's pressure pins at ~1.0. Arms carry the flipped one-head reference (iteration 32).

certification_fp64_exact_labels.note: float64 autograd through the closed-form fields at the sample query points, worst over 5 seeds per split; the momentum row verifies the rotational Bernoulli derivation itself. Thresholds: momentum <= 1e-10, incompressibility <= 1e-12, Helmholtz <= 1e-10 (tests/test_euler_rotational.py)

protocol.capacity: one-head flipped reference (heads=1, ranks 48/16); singpair kernel dictionary; multi-field output {velocity:1, pressure:0}

wall_confirmation.pre_registered: the field_mode='linear' arm is exactly odd in the boundary-velocity drive; the pressure target is exactly even (drive-quadratic); the drive distribution is negation-symmetric; therefore its pressure relative L2 must pin at ~1.0 on every split and seed

iteration_35_declared_degree.design: Iteration 35: the DECLARED-degree fix rung of the nonlinear-fragility ladder (diagnosis: iteration 34, results/nonlinear_fragility_2026-07-04.json -- both nonlinear-mode extrapolation blowups share one engine, the multiplicative zero-preserving read-in's implicit drive degree ~21 against targets of exactly degree 1 and 2).  Fix mirrors how the architecture declares linearity: MeshTransformer(field_mode='quadratic') -- drive-linear machinery end to end (drive lift, LinearMeshFieldBlock stack, linear kernel decode) plus EXACTLY ONE bilinear operator-conditioned typed composition at the query read-in (QuadraticFieldReadIn, the third field-mode class), so the output is an exact degree-<=2 polynomial in the drive for any weights.  Arms mt_singpair_q2 on both suites (3 seeds x 3000 steps, jobs p24_*); typed addendum mt_singpair_q2_pseudo on euler_bernoulli (declared degree AND declared parity, jobs p24_eb_q2p_*) because the untyped arm's circulation-OOD is capped by the iteration-23 parity floor (~0.647), a mechanism orthogonal to degree.  Acceptance study: studies/declared_degree.py, artifact results/declared_degree_2026-07-05.json.

iteration_36_navier_stokes.design: Iteration 36: the first SOLVER-LABELED suite on a genuinely nonlinear PDE -- steady incompressible Navier-Stokes (-nu lap u + (u.grad)u + grad p = 0, div u = 0), Taylor-Hood P2-P1 with analytic-Jacobian Newton (datasets/fem_navier_stokes.py), on the bank's star domains with a smooth band-limited TANGENTIAL boundary velocity on an arc (exact continuous compatibility by construction) and Re = 1/nu as the family parameter (operator scalar fed to arms: viscosity = 1/Re).  Fixed-dataset regime (dataset_train_ns.py), 15 epochs, seeds 17/29/43.
caveats: the 1e-6 MMS bar is met at h=0.01 (6.2e-7); production labels run at h=0.02 (MMS 4.7e-6) where the finer-mesh label-noise floor -- the bound that matters against ~1e-2 model errors -- is reported per split in the manifest

(1) The Re<=1 discriminating band: supplementary catalog slice ns_cavity_star/v1-lowre (180 cases, Re log-uniform [0.5, 5] with eval_unseen_Re at (5, 10]; same geometry/drive family, same h = 0.0105 and verification discipline, via the new --reynolds-range slice mechanism), linear and nl_pseudo arms at the fixed-dataset protocol (15 epochs, seeds 17/29/43); the per-case velocity gap joins the archived iteration-36 curve into one Re 0.5-300 measurement, completing the pre-registered P1 velocity leg.  (2) The N-S operator-fidelity block: dataset_train_ns.py now emits the strong-form momentum residual of the model's own prediction (nu~ lap u - (u.grad)u - grad p, float64 autograd, 32 interior queries, 2 cases/split, normalized by the prediction's advection norm; nu~ = 1/Re read from the CASE -- the model never sees the PDE, the metric does) plus the divergence norm, instrument-certified in-tree against the exact Kovasznay solution (scores ~0 only when the case viscosity is used) and a rigid rotation with dropped pressure (scores exactly 1).

protocol.comparators: mt_singpair_linear / mt_singpair_nl_pseudo reports from iterations 36 (v1) and 37 (v1-lowre), re-aggregated at identical binning

joined_gap_vs_re.note: gap = arm minus nl_pseudo per-case mean per log-Re bin, seeds 17/29/43 pooled, eval_id + eval_unseen_Re; the join is between two separately trained catalogs (108- vs 840-case train splits) -- the GAP is the internally controlled measure on each side, absolute levels are not comparable across the join

iteration_38_confound_check.rule: REVISION outcome: bottom joined bin velocity gap (linear_pseudo minus nl_pseudo) <= 0.05 means the iteration-37 deficit was parity/capacity and its velocity reading is REVISED; STANDS outcome (falsifier of the revision): bottom gap >= 0.1 means the read-in-class reading stands, now unconfounded; between 0.05 and 0.1: partial closure

caveats: the linear_pseudo arm matches nl_pseudo's pseudo sector but not its full parameter count (131,248 vs 233,108): the remaining difference is the nonlinear read-in stack itself, which is the treatment variable, but a pure width-matched linear control at 233k params was not run
the two sides of the joined curve are separately trained catalogs (108- vs 840-case train splits); only gaps cross the Re = 10 join
the archived iteration-36 v1 comparator reports predate the fidelity block, so the v1-side fidelity columns exist only for the new arm
